introduction: On this first day of the new year, the octave day of Christmas, we honour Mary as the Holy Mother of God. Since 1968 the Church has also kept this day as the World Day of Peace. The first reading gives us the ancient blessing of the priests of Israel, and in the Gospel Mary treasures all that has happened, pondering it in her heart. As we begin the year, let us place it under God's blessing and Mary's care.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: At the start of this new year, let us entrust our hopes and needs to God, through the prayers of Mary, the Mother of God.
intentions: For the Church: that, like Mary, she may treasure God's word and bring Christ to the world in this new year. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace among nations and peoples: that leaders may choose dialogue instead of violence, and that every life may be protected. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who begin this year in sorrow, sickness or uncertainty: that the Lord may make his face shine on them and give them peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For mothers and for all who care for children: that they may be blessed and supported in their work. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish and our families: that every day of this year may be lived in God's grace. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, through the Virgin Mary you gave us the Saviour of the world. Bless us at the start of this year, keep us in your peace, and hear the prayers we make. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: She kept these things in her heart
reflection.body:
The new year begins with a blessing. In the first reading God tells Moses how the priests are to bless the people: "The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace." It is a wonderful prayer to say over our families as the year begins.

Today the Church honours Mary with her greatest title: Mother of God. In 431 the Council of Ephesus defended this name, not first to praise Mary but to protect the truth about Jesus. The child born of Mary is not merely a man in whom God dwells; he is the eternal Son of God made flesh. So Mary is truly the Mother of God.

Paul puts the mystery in a few words: "when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman." And the result is our adoption: "because you are children, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, 'Abba, Father!'" Because God's Son became Mary's son, we can become sons and daughters of God.

In the Gospel, the shepherds hurry to Bethlehem, find the child, and tell everyone what the angels said. People are amazed. But Mary does something quieter: "Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart." She does not understand everything, but she keeps it, turns it over in prayer, and waits for God to make it clear.

That is a good way to begin a new year. We do not know what this year will bring: joys, trials, changes we cannot foresee. Like Mary, we can receive each event, keep it in our hearts, and look for God in it.

On this World Day of Peace, let us also pray for peace in our world and become peacemakers ourselves, in our homes, our workplaces and our communities.
